```
Manage teams and team membership.

Teams provide hierarchical grouping of users and workspaces. Teams can be
nested up to 3 levels deep (e.g., /engineering/backend/api).

Usage:
  spin team [flags]
  spin team [command]

Available Commands:
  create      Create a new team
  delete      Delete a team
  get         Get team details
  list        List teams
  member      Manage team members
  policy      Manage the network policies a team's workspaces may run under
  secret      Manage the secrets the egress proxy adds for a team's workspaces

Flags:
  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for team

Global Flags:
      --config string        config file (default is $HOME/.spin/config.yaml)
  -o, --output string        text for a person, or json: one document of what the API answered, and no prose (default "text")
      --profile string       named profile to use; SPIN_PROFILE names it when this flag does not (default "default")
      --traceparent string   the W3C traceparent of the span this command is part of; its own span is sent to the installation unless the profile says telemetry: false

Use "spin team [command] --help" for more information about a command.
```

### spin team create

```
Create a new team. Use --parent to nest under an existing team.

Examples:
  spin team create engineering
  spin team create backend --parent engineering
  spin team create api --parent /engineering/backend

Usage:
  spin team create <name> [flags]

Flags:
      --description string   Team description
  -h, --help[=true|false]    help for create
      --parent string        Parent team ID or path
      --slug string          URL-friendly slug (auto-generated if empty)

### spin team delete

```
Delete a team. Only team owners can delete teams.
Teams with children cannot be deleted unless --recursive is used.

### spin team policy

```
A team's network policies are named allowlists, declared by its admins where the
installation lets teams declare them, for the workspaces of the team and of the teams below it.
A workspace runs under one by naming it (spin workspace create --network-tag, spin workspace
retag). They only allow: a brokered rule is the installation's to declare.

Usage:
  spin team policy [flags]
  spin team policy [command]

Available Commands:
  delete      Delete a team's network policy no workspace runs under
  list        List a team's network policies and what each allows
  set         Make a team's policy, or replace what it allows

Flags:
  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for policy

Global Flags:
      --config string        config file (default is $HOME/.spin/config.yaml)
  -o, --output string        text for a person, or json: one document of what the API answered, and no prose (default "text")
      --profile string       named profile to use; SPIN_PROFILE names it when this flag does not (default "default")
      --traceparent string   the W3C traceparent of the span this command is part of; its own span is sent to the installation unless the profile says telemetry: false

Use "spin team policy [command] --help" for more information about a command.
```

#### spin team policy set

```
Make a team's policy, or replace what it allows, whole. Each --rule is destinations, then
the ports they are reached on after a colon: CIDRs or addresses, and names - exact or with one
leading "*." - separated by commas. No ports is every port; no destinations is any destination
on those ports. No --rule at all allows nothing.

Example:
  spin team policy set <team> builds --rule github.com,*.githubusercontent.com:443 --rule 10.20.0.0/16:5432

Usage:
  spin team policy set <team> <name> [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for set
      --rule stringArray    Destinations and ports, as dest,dest:port,port (repeatable)

Global Flags:
      --config string        config file (default is $HOME/.spin/config.yaml)
  -o, --output string        text for a person, or json: one document of what the API answered, and no prose (default "text")
      --profile string       named profile to use; SPIN_PROFILE names it when this flag does not (default "default")
      --traceparent string   the W3C traceparent of the span this command is part of; its own span is sent to the installation unless the profile says telemetry: false
```

### spin team secret

```
A team's secrets are what a brokered network rule has the host's egress proxy add to a
request a workspace of the team makes - an API key the workspace uses without ever holding it.
A value is set and replaced, and not shown again; it is sent only to the hosts set with it. A
workspace of a sub-team uses the nearest of its teams that has the name. The installation's
admins, who write the policies, are trusted with it.

Usage:
  spin team secret [flags]
  spin team secret [command]

Available Commands:
  delete      Delete a team's secret
  list        List a team's secrets, by name
  set         Set a team's secret, read from standard input or kept in Secrets Manager or Parameter Store

Flags:
  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for secret

Global Flags:
      --config string        config file (default is $HOME/.spin/config.yaml)
  -o, --output string        text for a person, or json: one document of what the API answered, and no prose (default "text")
      --profile string       named profile to use; SPIN_PROFILE names it when this flag does not (default "default")
      --traceparent string   the W3C traceparent of the span this command is part of; its own span is sent to the installation unless the profile says telemetry: false

Use "spin team secret [command] --help" for more information about a command.
```

#### spin team secret set

```
Set a team's secret to what standard input holds, and the hosts it may be sent to, replacing
what the name held. Read from standard input and never an argument: an argument is in every
process listing on the machine. A brokered rule that injects the secret and names any host not
given here is refused it.

With --ref the team keeps the value in Secrets Manager or Parameter Store instead, and the control
plane reads it as the team whenever a host asks: the secret or the parameter must carry the tag
spin-team-id with the team's id. A parameter costs nothing; a SecureString is opened on the read.

Example:
  printf %s "$GITHUB_TOKEN" | spin team secret set engineering github --host api.github.com
  spin team secret set engineering github --host api.github.com \
    --ref arn:aws:secretsmanager:us-east-2:123456789012:secret:github-AbCdEf

Usage:
  spin team secret set <team> <name> [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for set
      --host stringArray    A host the secret may be sent to, named exactly (repeatable)
      --ref string          The ARN of the Secrets Manager secret or the Parameter Store parameter the team keeps the value in

Global Flags:
      --config string        config file (default is $HOME/.spin/config.yaml)
  -o, --output string        text for a person, or json: one document of what the API answered, and no prose (default "text")
      --profile string       named profile to use; SPIN_PROFILE names it when this flag does not (default "default")
      --traceparent string   the W3C traceparent of the span this command is part of; its own span is sent to the installation unless the profile says telemetry: false
```
